notes.title: Update EA v1.4.2f1 and free environment add-on
notes.notes:
I’m currently working towards releasing the “full” version of Vinyl Reality and leaving Early Access, but I though it would be a good idea to release a small update in the meantime, with a couple of improvements and a new environment add-on.

[h2]Kratfwerk Environment[/h2]
Some users who have been using Vinyl Reality from its early beginnings might remember the old main menu scene located in a large industrial hall which was loosely based on [url=https://kraftwerkberlin.de/de/]Kraftwerk[/url] in Berlin. Since I really liked the layout and atmosphere of this space, I decided to convert it to an audio reactive environment designed for streaming.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31209528/720d8ea812e08d06d3b0c9a8d9fc14e6b5d2e4ce.jpg[/img]

This environment is [u][b]not[/b][/u] included with the application by default, but can be [b][url=https://vinylreality.mod.io/kraftwerk]downloaded from mod.io[/url][/b].

Be sure to also check out some of the other amazing environments which have been created by the community on [url=https://vinylreality.mod.io]Vinyl Reality's mod.io page[/url]!

[h2]Other notable improvements:[/h2][list]
[*] [b]Beat Detection[/b]: Improved accuracy and responsiveness for all audio reactive components
[*] [b]LIV:[/b] Updated SDK to v1.5.3. Be sure to use [u][b]LIV’s latest public beta[/b][/u] for the best experience
[*] [b]Desktop Mirror:[/b] Added optional [b][url=https://vinyl-reality.com/wiki/doku.php?id=application_settings#desktop_mirror]bass vibration effect[/url][/b]
[*] [b]Streaming Console:[/b] Added[b] [url=https://vinyl-reality.com/wiki/doku.php?id=streaming_console#keyboard_shortcuts]keyboard shortcuts[/url][/b] for selecting cameras
[*] [b]Tech:[/b] Improved performance and fixed several minor bugs
[/list]

notes.title: Update EA v1.4.1f1
notes.notes:
This update fixes a couple of bugs and adds several small improvements.

[h2]Breaking Changes[/h2]

To simplify its installation, the directory for [b]custom content[/b] (ex: environments, slipmats) has been moved to: [u]C:\\Users\\YourUsername\\Documents\\Vinyl Reality[/u]

Content that’s already been installed will have to be [b]copied manually[/b] from the old to the new directory, or reinstalled.

For more information on how to install custom content, please refer to the [url=https://vinyl-reality.com/wiki/doku.php?id=custom_content]online documentation[/url].

notes.title: Mod.io page for sharing User Generated Content & Attic environment re-release
notes.notes:
[h2]Mod.io[/h2]

To make it easier to [b]share, discover and download user generated content[/b] for Vinyl Reality, I’ve setup a page for the application on [url=https://vinylreality.mod.io/]mod.io[/url], a cross platform mod API.

Content creators will be encouraged to upload their content to this page going forward, so that all of the [b]custom environments and slipmats[/b] for Vinyl Reality are [b]easily accessible in one place[/b]. An account is [u][b]not[/b][/u] needed to download content, but is required to upload it.

All of the custom content for Vinyl Reality can now be found at: [b][url=https://vinylreality.mod.io/]https://vinylreality.mod.io/[/url][/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31209528/b62bc930eecce0ef877c8a722b7c59cf228e4851.jpg[/img]

[h3]Installing custom content[/h3]

For the time being, installing user generated content, still requires the files to be [b]downloaded manually[/b] from the mod.io page, and then [b]extracted and copied into the correct directory[/b].

[b]Install instructions for custom content[/b] can be found on the [b][url=https://vinyl-reality.com/wiki/doku.php?id=custom_content]documentation wiki[/url][/b].

I hope to be able to integrate the mod.io API into Vinyl Reality at some point though, so that in the future content can be browsed and managed directly from inside the application.

[h2]Attic Environment[/h2]

Some users might fondly remember the Attic environment which was included in [b]early versions[/b] of Vinyl Reality, but was replaced by the Black Box and Streaming Studio in a recent update.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31209528/4efbbbf9cb8263570b6f1e5dff872e373a51aee5.jpg[/img]

After making a few tweaks, this environment is now available again as a [b]separate add-on[/b] and can also be downloaded from the mod.io page: https://vinylreality.mod.io/attic

notes.title: Update EA v1.2.4
notes.notes:
Early Access version 1.2.4 of Vinyl Reality is now available. This update adds the final improvements to the record case before the upcoming full release of the application.

[h1]Vinyl Record Labels[/h1]
My favorite new feature in this update is the ability to load and display the [b]cover art[/b] embedded in audio files on the[b] vinyl record’s label[/b]. I think it adds a really nice visual touch to the records and makes each one feel more unique and recognizable. 

If no front cover art image is embedded in a file, the old default record label will be used. As always, this feature is optional and can be configured in the new record case user settings panel.

[h1]Additional Metadata[/h1]
I’ve redesigned the bottom part of the record case’s UI and replaced the mostly useless navigation menu options UI with a display for the selected track's [b]key[/b], [b]length[/b] and [b]genre[/b] metadata.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31209528/1933d3a7537de0c5224907885d601d7089869b9c.jpg[/img]

Additionally, when a track is loaded onto a turntable, it’s key can also be displayed on the turntable’s pitch slider (pictured above), making it easier to [b]mix harmonically[/b].
Because a change in pitch also changes the key of the track, the key’s value will change color to indicate that the key has changed if the pitch is adjusted by [b]more than 3 percent[/b].

[h1]Full Release Notes[/h1]
I’ve also added a number of other changes and improvements, so be sure to read through the full release notes below.
[list]
[*] [b]Record Case:[/b] Added option to display cover art embedded in audio file on vinyl record label
[*] [b]Record Case:[/b] Replaced navigation menu options UI with display for the selected track's key, length and genre metadata
[*] [b]Record Case:[/b] Added ability to browse entire Rekordbox Collection after loading exported XML
[*] [b]Record Case:[/b] Changed save location for audio recordings to separate "Recordings" subfolder
[*] [b]Turntable:[/b] Added option to display current track's key on pitch slider UI
[*] [b]Turntable:[/b] Added ability to load separate slipmat images for left (Slipmat_Left.png) and right (Slipmat_Right.png) turntable
[*] [b]User Settings:[/b] Added separate record case UI panel
[*] [b]Bug:[/b] Fixed potential memory leak in record case
[*] [b]Demo Tracks:[/b] Added 4 new tracks, courtesy of [url=http://www.foldrecords.be]Fold Records[/url]
[/list]

For more in-depth information about all of these features, you can check out the online documentation: https://vinyl-reality.com/wiki

notes.title: Update EA v1.2.2 – Audio Reactive lighting added to SDK
notes.notes:
After a short summer break, I’m getting back up to speed with releasing new updates for Vinyl Reality. 

This latest update focuses on adding new functionality to Vinyl Reality’s [b]Unity SDK[/b]. 
Custom environments created with the SDK can now also contain [b]lights which react to the music that is playing[/b], similar to the lights in the built-in club environment. 

This update gives content creators a lot of new tools and creative freedom to design amazing and more dynamic custom environments, and I’m really excited to see what kind of environments the Vinyl Reality community will create using these new SDK features!

[h1]Getting Started[/h1]

If you want to start creating your own environments for Vinyl Reality, grab the latest version of the SDK from the Vinyl Reality website: https://vinyl-reality.com/sdk/

If you’re interested in trying out some of the amazing environments created by other members of the community, the Vinyl Reality Discord server has a channel which lists all of the available environments: https://discord.gg/tQ7cNR4


[h1]Full Release Notes[/h1]
[list]
[*] [b]SDK:[/b] Released v1.3 which adds audio reactive lighting to custom environments
[*] [b]Tech:[/b] Updated Unity to version 2018.4.5f1

notes.title: Update EA v1.2.1 – Turntable customization and improvements
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31209528/d3f7b6f8d238625b171c16bb3bf86ad0e9d58297.jpg[/img]

Version 1.2.1 of Vinyl Reality is now available. This update adds a ton of settings which allows user to customize both the appearance and handling of the turntables.

[h1]Customizing the turntable’s appearance[/h1]

The appearance of the turntables can now be customized in a number of ways. 
First of all, there a re now two turntable color schemes to chose from, the classic dark (SL-1210) scheme and the new light (SL-1200) scheme also found in earlier version of Vinyl Reality.

Users can now also easily design and load their own slipmat designs by following this handy guide available on the  [url=https://vinyl-reality.com/wiki/doku.php?id=how_to_create_and_load_a_custom_slipmat_design]online documentation website.[/url]

[h1]Turntable handling settings[/h1]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31209528/ea32c53cd6be5ba1b3b47eb109b512947e6f5a34.jpg[/img]

The user settings menu now has a separate turntable panel, which allows users to configure how the turntables handle. 
For example, setting the [b]Slipmat Friction[/b] to high and the [b]Motor Start / Stop Speed[/b] to instant, will make the turntables handle a lot more like a [u][b]CDJ[/b][/u] (in vinyl mode) than a regular turntable. 

[h1]Turntable spindle input[/h1]

The turntable’s spindle can now also be used to make precise pitch bend corrections. 
To increase or decrease the playback speed using the spindle, first grab the spindle with the trigger (index finger) and then [u][b]while grabbing[/b][/u] slide the thumb up or down the controller’s trackpad, or move the controller’s joystick up or down. 

[h1]Full Release Notes[/h1]

I’ve also added a number of other changes and small improvements, so be sure to read through the full release notes below. For more in-depth information about all of these features, you can check out the online documentation: https://vinyl-reality.com/wiki

[list]
[*] [b]Turntable:[/b] Added ability to pitch bend using spindle
[*] [b]Turntable:[/b] Added ability to load custom slipmat designs
[*] [b]Turntable:[/b] Added user setting to chose between light and dark color schemes
[*] [b]Turntable:[/b] Added user setting for slipmat friction
[*] [b]Turntable:[/b] Added user setting for motor start / stop speed
[*] [b]Turntable:[/b] Added user setting for motor power-off speed
[*] [b]Turntable:[/b] Added user setting for platter pitch bend sensitivity
[*] [b]Turntable:[/b] Added user setting for spindle pitch bend sensitivity
[*] [b]Mixer:[/b] Changed control knob input method for joystick
[*] [b]User Settings:[/b] Added "Re-center Position" button to application settings panel
[*] [b]SteamVR:[/b] Added optional "Re-center Position" input action to controller bindings

notes.title: Update EA v1.2.0 – Valve Index and Oculus Rift S controller support
notes.notes:
Version 1.2.0 of Vinyl Reality is now available. This update adds support for several new controller types, including Valve’s Index controllers and the Oculus Rift S.

[h1]Index Controller Support[/h1]

I have [b]not [/b]yet finished the skeletal input system, which would use finger tracking and touch to interact with objects, so for now the Index controllers still use the same input input system as other controllers.
The control scheme for the Index controllers has been designed to be as intuitive and reliable as possible, but you can always modify it to your personal preferences using the SteamVR controller bindings settings.

I’ve made the “experimental” (and outdated) branch of the application, which contains an [b]unfinished[/b] implementation of the skeletal input system, public for every one who already owns a pair of index controllers to try out. If there is enough interest, I might continue working on the skeletal input version of the application at a later date, so be sure to let me know in the comments below!

[h1]Trackpad input tweaks for mixer knobs[/h1]

I’ve also changed the way rotary knobs on the mixer (ex: EQ knobs) react to trackpad input. To rotate a knob with the trackpad, you now first need to [b]grab the knob[/b] and then slide your thumb [b]up or down[/b] the trackpad. This action mimics rotating the knob between your thumb and index finger and should feel more natural.

I’ve also added two new trackpad related settings to the mixer’s user settings panel: 
[list]
[*] [b]Invert Left Trackpad Input:[/b]
Inverts the direction the knob rotates for the left controller’s trackpad
[*] [b]Trackpad Scroll Range:[/b] 
Controls how many degrees the knob rotates based on the trackpad input
[/list]

[h1]Full Release notes:[/h1]
[list]
[*] [b]SteamVR version:[/b] Added support for Valve’s Index controllers
[*] [b]Oculus version:[/b] Updated plug-ins to display correct controller models for Rift S
[*] [b]Oculus version:[/b] Fixed haptic feedback (again)
[*] [b]Mixer:[/b] Updated trackpad input for rotary knobs
[*] [b]Mixer:[/b] Added user settings for rotary knob trackpad input
[*] [b]Tutorial:[/b] Added input action hints to controllers
[/list]

notes.title: Update EA v1.1.9 – Mixer Fader improvements
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31209528/24123d0a600d3e37c21b1333b0eed476ea571143.jpg[/img]

[b]Version 1.1.9[/b] of Vinyl Reality is now available. This update focuses on improving the functionality of the mixer’s crossfader and channel faders by making them more configurable.

[h1]Mixer Fader Settings[/h1]

A new Mixer Fader Settings panel has been added to the user settings interface. Using this panel, the [b]curves of both the crossfader and channel faders[/b] can be adjusted to adapt to different play styles or situations. 

For example, scratch DJs often prefer a crossfader with a very sharp curve for performing fast cuts, while radio DJs might prefer a smooth crossfader curve which maintains a constant output volume while fading between two tracks.

Both fader curves are displayed and updated in real-time to visualize the current settings. The curve describes [b]the volume (y-axis)[/b] in relation to the [b]fader’s position (x-axis)[/b].

Each of the mixer’s channels can now also be [b]assigned to either the left or right side of the crossfader[/b], or set to ignore the crossfader’s position completely.

[h1]Audio Settings[/h1]

I’ve also slightly redesigned the Audio Settings panel and replaced the Advanced settings with an Audio Buffer Size setting, which offers users [b]more granular control[/b] than previously. This can be useful if the recommended settings still causes a delay between the default and master audio outputs.

For more more [b]in-depth information[/b] about these features, be sure to check out the relevant online documentation: https://vinyl-reality.com/wiki/doku.php?id=user_settings

[h1]Full Release notes[/h1]
[list]

[*] [b]Mixer:[/b] Added crossfader assign settings
[*] [b]User Settings:[/b] Redesigned audio buffer settings to give users more granular control
[*] [b]User Set- tings:[/b] Improved UI lay-out and responsiveness
[*] [b]SDK:[/b] Fixed issue with terrain shaders not being loaded for custom environments
[*] [b]Bug Fixes:[/b] Several minor bug fixes and improvements

notes.title: Update EA v1.1.8 – Mixer Equalizer improvements
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31209528/097d42d4651c80a6ff3beac0bcb91df9eb501f7e.jpg[/img]

[b]Version 1.1.8[/b] of Vinyl Reality is now available. This update focuses on improving the functionality of the mixer’s [b]3 band equalizer[/b] as well as fixing some major bugs in the main menu.

[h1]Equalizer kill switches[/h1]
Each of the mixer’s 3 band equalizer knobs now has a kill switch function which when activated [b]cuts all the frequencies[/b] for the corresponding range (High, Mid or Low) from the audio signal playing through the channel. This effect can also be achieved by turning an equalizer knob all the way counter-clockwise, but the kill switch function allows for[b] fast and easy toggling.[/b]

While the kill switch is active, a [b]LED ring[/b] on the bottom of the equalizer knob will [b]illuminate[/b]. If the knob is turned while the kill switch is active, the LED ring will [b]flash [/b]to indicate that the adjustment has no effect.

[h1]Equalizer settings[/h1]
The frequency crossover points (Low to Mid and Mid to High) and crossover slope of the mixer’s 3 band equalizer can now be configured using the new mixer settings panel inside the user settings UI. Tweaking these values can be useful to adapt the equalizer to different musical genres.

For more information about how to use the new kill switch function and equalizer settings, be sure to check out the wiki page on the topic: https://vinyl-reality.com/wiki/doku.php?id=mixer

[h1]Full Release notes[/h1]
[list]
[*] [b]Mixer: [/b]Added kill switch function to 3 band equalizer
[*] [b]Mixer: [/b]Added mixer settings panel to configure 3 band equalizer
[*] [b]Bug Fix:[/b] Fixed crash in main menu affecting some users
[*] [b]Bug Fix:[/b] Fixed main menu sometimes becoming unresponsive
[/list]

notes.title: Update EA v1.1.7 – Further record case improvements
notes.notes:
[b]Version 1.1.7 [/b]of Vinyl Reality is now available. This update adds a bunch of improvements and new functionality to the record case. 

The record case now [b]automatically keeps tracks of which records have already been played[/b] and will mark them accordingly. When a track is played on one of the turntables and the output volume of the corresponding mixer channel is above a certain threshold (0.1), it will be marked in yellow in the record case’s UI.

Upon ending a session and exiting the environment (or closing the application), the history of all the tracks played will automatically be [b]exported as a M3U8 playlist[/b] and saved in the[b] “Vinyl Reality/History”[/b] subfolder in the user’s default music folder (ex: [i]…/Users/username/My Music/Vinyl Reality/History[/i]).

These playlist can then be loaded into Vinyl Reality afterwards like any other playlist. The order of the tracks in the playlist [b]matches the order in which they were originally played[/b].

Be sure to check out the full release notes below to see what other new features have been added!

[h1]Upcoming features poll[/h1]

To help me decide [b]which features of the application to focus on in the upcoming updates[/b], I’ve organized a small poll in the [url=https://discord.gg/9TCsXfc]Vinyl Reality discord server[/url]. 
If you want your voice to be heard, be sure to join the Discord server and cast your vote [b]by the beginning of next week[/b]!


[h1]Full Release notes[/h1]
[list]
[*] [b]Record Case:[/b] Tracks that have already been played are now marked in yellow
[*] [b]Record Case: [/b]Track history is exported to a M3U8 playlist upon exiting environment

notes.title: Update EA v1.1.6 - Rekordbox integration and more
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31209528/d1564d980101ef6de001ea32bb44f6f0f0ae3942.png[/img]
[b]Version 1.1.6[/b] of Vinyl Reality is now available. 

The biggest feature added in this update is the ability to load Rekordbox collections into Vinyl Reality. For those who aren’t familiar with the software, Rekordbox is a free music management and DJ app from Pioneer DJ.

Being able to load a Rekordbox collection into Vinyl Reality has many advantages, including:
[list]
[*] [b]All meta data[/b] can be read directly from the Rekordbox collection, including the BPM value
[*] [b]Folder hierarchy and playlists[/b] are synced between Rekordbox and Vinyl Reality
[*] Only a single music collection needs to be managed and [b]all analysis[/b] can be done inside Rekordbox
[/list]

For details on how to load a Rekordbox collection, be sure to read the new [url=https://vinyl-reality.com/wiki/doku.php?id=how_to_load_a_rekordbox_collection]guide on the wiki page[/url].

This update also includes a lot of other small improvements and bug fixes, so be sure to check out the full release notes below!

[h1]Full release notes[/h1]
[list]
[*] [b]Record Case:[/b] Added support for loading Rekordbox collection in XML format
[*] [b]Record Case:[/b] Added shortcut to demo tracks in the record case’s root folder
[*] [b]Record Case:[/b] Fixed issue where the wrong item would be selected when returning
[*] [b]Record Case:[/b] Fixed sorting issue between audio files with different file formats
[*] [b]Mixer:[/b] Added 0dB mark to master VU meter
[*] [b]LIV:[/b] Fixed virtual headphones not working when LIV was enabled
[*] [b]LIV:[/b] Hid user avatar from LIV mixed reality camera
[*] [b]Main Menu:[/b] Added credits page
[*] [b]Main Menu:[/b] Added exit button to navigation menu
[*] [b]Meta:[/b] Added 2 new demo tracks
[/list]

notes.title: Update EA v1.1.5 – Bits and Bobs
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31209528/e1f26c068d70b2c9bc82bc62b5befab605754c34.jpg[/img]
[b]Version 1.1.5[/b] of Vinyl Reality is now available. This update adds a lot of small features and improvements across the application. 

[h1]Record Case Table[/h1]

An often requested feature was to make the height of the record case adjustable, so I’ve added an adjustable table for the record case to all environments. The angle of the record case’s lid can also be adjusted by grabbing it at the top. This should make the application more ergonomic for all users and also allow it to be used from a seated position. 

[h1]Streaming Console Auto-Switching[/h1]

The streaming console now also has an auto-switch feature, which will automatically toggle between different camera perspectives in sync with the music. For more details on how to use this new feature, please refer to the manual, or the newly created [url=https://vinyl-reality.com/wiki/doku.php?id=streaming_console#auto-switching]Vinyl Reality Wiki page on the topic[/url]. 

The plan is to add more topics to the Wiki in the coming weeks.

[h1]LIV Mixed Reality Capture[/h1]

The LIV SDK  has also been integrated into the SteamVR version of Vinyl Reality, which should make it easier to create Mixed Reality videos. 

[h1]SDK update[/h1]

And last but not least, I’ve also released a new version of the SDK (v1.1), which enables the use of the streaming console (including spectator cameras) in user created environments. You can download the latest version of the SDK from the Vinyl Reality website: https://vinyl-reality.com/sdk/

If you’re keen on trying out some custom environments created using the SDK, be sure to download the Beach Party environment  (shown in the image at the top of this post) created by Praaly from his website: https://vr.praaly.fr/home.php

[h1]Full release notes[/h1]
[list]
[*] [b]Record Case:[/b] Added record case table with adjustable height
[*] [b]Record Case:[/b] Made angle of record case lid and UI adjustable
[*] [b]Streaming Console:[/b] Added auto-switching feature for spectator cameras
[*] [b]Environments:[/b] Redesigned parts of the Recording Studio environment
[*] [b]Environments:[/b] Re-positioned spectator cameras in the Recording Studio environment
[*] [b]Tech:[/b] Integrated LIV SDK for Mixed Reality capture (SteamVR version only)
[*] [b]Tech:[/b] Updated SteamVR plugin to v2.2.0
[*] [b]SDK:[/b] Released v1.1 of the Vinyl Reality environment SDK
[/list]

notes.title: Update EA v1.1.3 – Record case playlists and improvements
notes.notes:
[b]Version 1.1.3[/b] of Vinyl Reality is now available. This first update of the new year adds several improvements to the record case.

[h1]Playlists[/h1]

The biggest new feature is the ability to load [b]m3u and m3u8 playlists[/b] in the record case, which makes loading your track collection inside Vinyl Reality a lot easier. This format of playlists can be created in, and exported from, most DJ, media player and music management applications.

Here are a couple of possible use cases for playlists in Vinyl Reality:
[list]
[*] Creating playlists with tracks sorted by BPM, Artist, etc..
[*] Breaking up a large music collection into manageable chunks, without having to move files
[*] Transferring playlists between different apps
[/list]

If playlists files are found in the current directory, they will be displayed in the record case list beneath the directories. To load a playlist, simply select it and use the enter action to open it. If an audio file included in a playlist is missing, it will be marked red in the record case list.

[h1]Performance[/h1]

I’ve also spent a lot of time improving the performance of the record case. In previous versions, loading folders or playlists which contain a large amount of tracks could take a long time, but with this update it should be almost instantaneous.

[h1]Full release notes:[/h1]
[list]
[*] [b]Record Case:[/b] Added support for loading m3u and m3u8 playlists
[*] [b]Record Case:[/b] Improved performance when loading a large amount of tracks
[*] [b]Record Case: [/b]Fixed some tags not being parsed correctly
[*] [b]Tech:[/b] Updated 3rd party libraries
[*] [b]Bug Fix:[/b] Fixed record sometimes not appearing from sleeve when scrolling through records
[/list]

notes.title: Update EA v1.1.2 – SteamVR Input
notes.notes:
Update 1.1.2 of Vinyl Reality has left the beta phase and is now available on the main branch. 

This update implements the new [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/250820/announcements/detail/3809361199426010680]SteamVR input system[/url], which allows you to setup an alternate control scheme for your controllers. The controller binding UI can be accessed in the headset through the SteamVR dashboard or on the desktop under the Devices menu in SteamVR.

Here’s an [b]overview [/b]of all the input actions that can be configured:

[list]
[*][b]Grab Pinch:[/b] Grab objects or input controls using the index finger (ex: sliders, knobs, etc..)
[*][b]Grap Grip:[/b] Grab objects or input controls using the entire hand (ex: vinyl records, etc…)
[*][b]Button Press:[/b] Press buttons (ex: start button, cue button, streaming console pads, etc…)
[*][b]Toggle Virtual Headphones:[/b] Toggle virtual headphones channel
[*][b]Joystick Position:[/b] Scroll through the record case list or make precise input control adjustments by moving the controller’s joystick
[*][b]Trackpad Slide:[/b] Scroll through the record case list or make precise input control adjustments by sliding the thumb over the controller’s trackpad [u](Requires Trackpad Position to be assigned)[/u]
[*][b]Trackpad Positon: [/b]Position of the thumb on the controller’s trackpad
[*][b]Record Case Open Menu: [/b]Open radial navigation menu in record case [u](Requires Trackpad Position to be assigned)[/u]
[*][b]Record Case Enter:[/b] Enter selected folder in record case
[*][b]Record Case Return:[/b] Return to previous folder in record case
[*][b]Toggle User Settings:[/b] Toggle user settings panel
[*][b]UI Click:[/b] Interact with UI elements in the main menu and user settings panels
[/list]

[h1]Full release notes:[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Feature:[/b] Added support for SteamVR input system
[*][b]Turntable:[/b] Fixed strobe dot speed on turntable platter
[*][b]Turntable: [/b]Reduced size and priority of turntable cartridge collider, to avoid accidentally grabbing it while reaching for the turntable's platter
[*][b]Environments: [/b]Removed creepy dude from club environment
[*][b]Tech:[/b] Rewrote input system to simplify implementation of different controller types
[*][b]Tech:[/b] Updated SteamVR plug-in to latest version
[*][b]Tech:[/b] Small performance improvements and tweaks
[*][b]Bug Fix:[/b] Fixed minor haptic feedback bugs
[*][b]Meta:[/b] Updated User Manual
[/list]

notes.title: Update EA v1.1.1 – Vinyl Reality SDK
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31209528/a6889624566611c18dcdb10e58de157305b4d767.jpg[/img]

[b]Version 1.1.1[/b] of Vinyl Reality is now available. This is quite a small update to the application itself, but I’m also releasing version 1.0 of the [b]Vinyl Reality SDK [/b]alongside it.

The Vinyl Reality SDK enables you to [b]create custom environments[/b] for Vinyl Reality inside the Unity Editor. It includes an example scene and all the components needed to setup your own Unity scene so that it can be loaded in Vinyl Reality. 

In this first version, the functionality is limited and only exposes control on spawning the user and placing all of the required DJ Gear, but future version of the SDK will gradually expose more functionality.

To get started creating your own environments, download the SDK and the documentation from the [url=https://vinyl-reality.com/sdk/]Vinyl Reality website[/url].

If you create an environment and want to share it with the rest of the Vinyl Reality community, be sure to post it on the [url=https://discord.gg/ZEJR8tU]SDK Discord channel![/url]
A more convenient way to share and install the environments from inside the application itself, will be added in the future.

Looking forward to seeing all of your creations!

[b]Full release notes:[/b]
[list]
[*] [b]General:[/b] Released SDK v1.0 for creating custom environments
[*] [b]General:[/b] Added “load custom content” panel to main menu to load user created content
[*] [b]General: [/b]Improved main menu design
[*] [b]Bug Fix: [/b]Possible fix for audio issues reported by some users
[/list]

notes.title: Update EA v1.0.7 – Native Oculus Rift support and more
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31209528/7b15cee8b65688b963035588c00ee89ac87ebc9a.png[/img]

[b]Version 1.0.7[/b] of Vinyl Reality has left the beta phase and is now available for everyone to try out.

This update adds [b]native support for the Oculus Rift[/b] headset and touch controllers, allowing Oculus users to run the application without SteamVR, resulting in better performance and an overall smoother experience. 
Another small bonus feature for Oculus users is that they now have a more lifelike 3rd person avatar, which is visible from the spectator cameras in the Recording Studio environment.

To launch the Oculus VR Mode, simple right click the application in your Steam library, and select the [i]Launch Vinyl Reality in Oculus VR Mode[/i] option.

For this update, I’ve also completely redesigned the main menu, to make it more user-friendly and visually appealing. 

Last but not least, all audio and application settings can now be accessed from inside VR, removing the need to take off your headset when configuring your settings. 
When running the application in Steam VR Mode, you can open the settings panel by pressing the menu button on the HTC Vive or Windows MR controllers, or by pressing the B or Y buttons on the Oculus touch controllers.
When running the application in Oculus VR Mode, the settings panel can be opened by pressing the start button on the left touch controller.

[b]Full Release Notes:[/b]
[list]
[*] General: Added native Oculus support
[*]General: Redesigned Main Menu UI and environment
[*]General: Redesigned loading screen
[*]User Settings: Made setting panels accessible in VR
[*]User Settings: Added dropdown selection for default audio device
[*]User Settings: Added button to set privacy preferences
[*]Interaction: Improved outlines for interactive objects
[*]Fixes: several small bug fixes and improvements
[*]Other: Hidden customization feature
[/list]      

Thanks again to all beta testers who helped test this new version ;)

notes.title: Update EA v1.0.6 – Polish and Performance
notes.notes:
Version 1.0.6 of Vinyl Reality has been released just in time for the weekend.

This update focuses on polishing existing features, and improving the overall performance of the application.

One of the biggest improvement is the addition of the “Minimize Master Output Delay” option in the advanced audio settings panel. Enabling this option should reduce the delay between the default and master audio outputs to a minimum, making it possible to mix using the speakers as a reference.

The turntable code has been completely rewritten to make it more robust, and to fix the issue where the playback position of records would drift. A small arrow has been added to the record label, which points to the turntable’s needle, when at the start of a track.

A lot of other code has also been rewritten, to make it easier to add new upcoming features. If I have done my job well, none of these code changes should not be noticeable, but in case you should encounter a new bug, be sure to report it.

[b]Full Release Notes:[/b]
[list]
[*]Audio Settings: Redesigned UI panel to be more clear 
[*]Audio Settings: Added experimental “Minimize Master Output Delay” option
[*]Audio Settings: Disabled master output by default
[*]Turntable: Fixed playback position drifting issue
[*]Vinyl Record: Fixed waveform not loading in certain edge cases
[/list]

Thanks to all beta testers who helped test this new version ;)

notes.title: Update EA v1.0.5 – Streaming Console
notes.notes:
Version 1.0.5 of Vinyl Reality is now available.

The goal of this update was to make footage recorded with Vinyl Reality more interesting and engaging for your audience to watch, by enabling you to select different camera perspectives to display on the desktop mirror, while recording or streaming your set.

You can switch between the different cameras by selecting the corresponding pad on the bottom row of the new streaming console. The leftmost pad, conveniently labeled [i]HMD[/i],  will display the feed from your headset.

To see what’s possible, be sure to check out this video that was recorded live using the features of the streaming console:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qTJo09_I7Dw

The streaming console also replaces the old audio recorder and adds some extra functionality, including a display which shows the duration and filename of the current recording. 

Please note that the record button on the streaming console [b]only records audio[/b] and [u][b]NOT[/b][/u] video. To record or stream video footage, it’s recommend to use an external tool like OBS Studio, which is free and easy to setup.

The streaming console is currently only available in the brand new [i]Recording Studio[/i] environment, which was designed to be as optimized as possible and should allow you to record your sessions without any performance issues. This environment also includes a screen which displays the feed from the external cameras when they’re activated.

For the next update (1.0.6) I don’t plan to add any new features, but instead I’ll be focusing on improving performance and polishing the content that is already there. This should give me a good foundation to start work on the next major update (1.1.0), which will add a new club environment with interactive light shows and special effects.

[b]Full Release Notes:[/b]
[list]
[*]Added streaming console
[*]Added Recording Studio environment
[*] Removed old audio recorder
[*]Optimized rendering performance
[/list]

If you record your set using the new features added in this update, be sure to share them in the Community Hub!

notes.title: Update EA v1.0.4 – Record Case improvements
notes.notes:
It took a bit longer than usual, but version 1.0.4 of Vinyl Reality is now available! 

This update focuses on improving the record case's functionality. New features include support for loading several new file formats and displaying track meta data, including BPM.

If a file contains meta data about the track's BPM (Beats Per Minute), this value can now be shown on the turntable's pitch slider. This can be a useful feature for beginners who want to for example practice their beatmatching techniques. This option can easily be disabled using the settings panel on the application's display mirror.

If a track does not yet contain BPM meta data, it can be added by analyzing it in an external application such as Traktor or MixMeister.

Due to the reading of meta data, opening folders which contain a lot of tracks will now take significantly longer than before, but this will be optimized in the next update. The next update will also add several tools to make streaming your Vinyl Reality sessions more interesting and entertaining. 

[b]Full release notes:[/b]
[list]
[*]Added support for loading FLAC, OGG, WAV, WMA and AIF file formats
[*]Record case UI now displays Artist, Title and BPM meta data instead of file name
[*]Added column to record case UI to display directory file count or track BPM value
[*]Added BPM to pitch slider UI
[*]Added BPM to record label
[*]Added BPM user settings panel to display mirror
[*]Added trackpad / thumbstick input for crossfader
[*]Improved readability of record case UI
[*]Improved readability of vinyl record grooves
[/list]

notes.title: Update EA v1.0.3 – Vinyl record grooves
notes.notes:
In previous versions of Vinyl Reality, the grooves displayed on the vinyl records were static and identical for each track. With this update, each track you play is analyzed, and the grooves of the record will accurately match the corresponding track's structure.

This makes it a lot easier to anticipate changes in the music, as you can easily spot breakdowns, drops and other elements by simply looking at the record. I believe that with the addition of these latest features, Vinyl Reality now offers a very solid and usable DJing experience in VR. 

The next update, which is scheduled to be released after the holidays, will focus on improving the record case's functionality and adding a BPM (Beats Per Minute) display. For more details, be sure to check out the [url=https://trello.com/b/hZeApOD8/steam-early-access-public-road-map]Early Access roadmap[/url]

[b]Full release notes:[/b]
[list]
[*]Visualized track structure on vinyl records
[*]Lowered minimum height of DJ workstation
[*]Increased amount of records to be stored in memory simultaneously
[*]Added tips to loading screen
[*]Minor bug fixes
[/list]

notes.title: Update EA v1.0.2 – DJ Workstation
notes.notes:
Version 1.0.2 of Vinyl Reality is now available. 

The main feature added in this update is the new DJ workstation, which allows users to adjust the height and angle of their DJ equipment. This should reduce neck strain caused by the weight of the VR headset after looking down at the DJ equipment for an extended period of time.

The DJ workstation is available in the Attic scene and can be controlled using the two handles in the center of the workstation’s top. The left handle controls the angle, and the handle on the right controls the height.

Some other small improvements have also been added:
[list]
[*]Replaced textures of turntable with a darker version, to reduce glare and eye strain
[*]Increased size of vinyl record trigger so they can picked up from the floor when dropped
[*]Exit sign now lights up when selected
[*]Improved audio signal flow
[/list]

notes.title: Added support for Oculus Rift and Touch controllers – Update EA v1.0.1
notes.notes:
I've just released version 1.0.1 of the application, which [b]adds support for the Oculus Rift and Touch controllers.[/b]

All of the input that used the Vive trackpad has been rewritten to work with the Oculus Touch controller's thumbstick or buttons. I've also added separate tutorial instructions for Oculus users, so be sure to go through it again if you've already completed it.

This new version also includes some small tweaks and fixes which affect none Oculus users as well.

[b]Full release notes:[/b]
[list]
[*]Added support for Oculus Rift and Touch controllers
[*]Added separate tutorial instructions for Oculus users
[*]Improved audio resampling quality
[*]Slightly reduced Vive trackpad sensitivity for turntable pitch slider
[/list]
